stages.label: 1481 Paris Missale Parisiense
stages.scope: Identified book witness and the Eucharistic components supported by the cited original leaves or edition-identified contents index; no complete reconstructed missal.
stages.summary: The 1481 Paris-use missal has a checked original colophon and bounded Maundy Thursday folios. Neither a first composition date for those prayers nor a predecessor relationship follows.

evidence.locus: Original scan PDF pp. 155–156, fol. lxix recto–verso, and p. 494 colophon; Usuarium book 79 contents pp. 152–180
evidence.claim: Original folios identify bounded Maundy Thursday prayer/rubric material; the colophon dates the Dupré and Huym printing to 22 September 1481.

stages.limitations: The scan and selected leaves do not certify full physical or textual completeness; 1685, 1705 and 1738 originals are uncollated. GW M24596 cites Ursula Baurmeister's study under 'Zur Datierung'; its full title, '1481: a false landmark in the history of French illustration?', and its place in a bibliographical society's transactions, vol. 11 (1996/99), pp. 350–403, were identified on 2026-10-22 from a bibliography index, but the article itself could not be read (no open copy found). The title suggests that the question concerns the dating of the book's illustration; the colophon year is kept as printed and remains flagged.
stages.reception: The local-use designation identifies the intended book tradition; actual adoption by every church and any continuing-use interval have not been established.

stages.label: 1496 Missale Cameracense, Higman for de Campis
stages.date_label: Penultimate day of February 1495 by the colophon (old style; 1496 new style)
stages.scope: One Paris print for Cambrai use; colophon and January calendar inspected.
stages.summary: The colophon states that this missal according to the use of the church of Cambrai was printed at Paris by Johann Higman at the expense of Johannes de Campis, with that church's customs and observances added, completed on the penultimate day of February 1495. The calendar carries Cambrai entries with folio references.

evidence.locus: DONum images 3 (January calendar) and 566 (colophon)
evidence.claim: Colophon and calendar inspected.

stages.limitations: The colophon year 1495 is old style (the Paris year then began at Easter), so the penultimate day of February 1495 falls in February 1496 by modern reckoning; GW gives 27/28 February 1495/96. The 1496 bounds express this conversion only, not a period of use. Not compared with the 1507 Lyon-held print, which was unavailable.
stages.reception: A manuscript note records purchase by an abbot named Gerard; diocesan use is not dated.

stages.label: 1738 Missale Parisiense, BnF B-178
stages.scope: Identified Paris-use missal edition and scholarly described Maundy Thursday postcommunion 1060; no original 1738 prayer body or whole-book text has been checked.
stages.witness_label: Missale Parisiense, 1738, BnF B-178; Usuarium book 7371
stages.summary: The exact BnF holding and year are catalogued. Ward discusses postcommunion 1060 in the 1738 Paris missal, while O’Connor’s MP annotation points to earlier Paris missals; neither establishes first introduction in 1738.

evidence.locus: Usuarium book 7371, identity fields: title, origin, age, shelfmark and Amiet 747
evidence.claim: Identifies a 1738 Paris missal edition and BnF B-178 holding.

evidence.locus: Notitiae 44 (2008), printed pp. 633–634, note 67: 1738MP 1060
evidence.claim: Identifies the Maundy Thursday postcommunion as no. 1060 in the edited 1738 Paris missal.

evidence.locus: Annotated orations, entry 1060 and abbreviation MP
evidence.claim: The aggregate MP source mark points to Paris missals of 1685 and 1705, leaving the first introduction unresolved.

stages.limitations: The original Gallica scan linked from Usuarium returned 403 in the earlier inventory research; the 1738 original and 1685/1705 comparators are uncollated. No prayer wording is transcribed here, no 1481-to-1738 revision is asserted, and the catalogue year is not an effective-use date.
stages.reception: Publication and later scholarly identification do not establish adoption in every Paris church, a first-use date or continued observance.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1728 Rouen missal witness and exposes a possible duplicate catalogue row.

stages.label: 1508 Saint-Ruf missal (Valence, Jean Belon and Pierre de Mole)
stages.date_label: Subscription: last day of April 1508 (transcribed by Chevalier, 1858)
stages.scope: One identified printing: subscription, physical make-up and Chevalier's description of its ceremonial content.
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum usum venerabilis abbatie canonicorum regularium Sancti Ruphi Valentie, Valence 1508 (Valence library copies described by Chevalier; catalogue witness 5825 = Mazarine 2° 1169 A)
stages.summary: Chevalier transcribes the subscription on the recto of the last leaf: the missal for the use of the abbey of Saint-Ruf, ordered and completed, was printed in Valence by Jean Belon and Pierre de Mole, partners, on the last day of April 1508; Belon's mark follows. He describes a quarto in red and black in three parts: 184 numbered leaves, an unnumbered 14-leaf Canon in very large type, and 120 leaves. He says the missal also contains, spread through its parts, the ceremonial proper to the abbey, drawn from the Ordinarium of G. de Nemauso, that of Abbot Lethbert and customs confirmed by general chapters.

evidence.locus: Printed p. 192 (image n205)
evidence.claim: Subscription transcribed: Valence, Jean Belon and Pierre de Mole, last day of April 1508; quarto, three parts with a 14-leaf Canon; contains the abbey's own ceremonial.

evidence.locus: Printed p. 193 (image n206)
evidence.claim: The ceremonial is drawn from the Ordinarium of G. de Nemauso, Abbot Lethbert's, and customs confirmed by general chapters; two of the three Valence copies keep the last leaves.

stages.limitations: Scholarly description only; the original was not viewed by this lane. Chevalier calls the book a quarto while the catalogue shelfmark (Mazarine 2°) suggests folio; copy identity with catalogue witness 5825 is assumed at edition level. The ceremonial's sources are Chevalier's attribution.
stages.reception: The book is titled for the abbey and order of Saint-Ruf; use in its dependent priories is not established.

stages.label: 1529 Saint-Victor missal (Paris, Nicolas Prévost)
stages.date_label: 1529 as cited by Legg; 15 September 1529 by Weale–Bohatta (title leaf not inspected)
stages.scope: Existence of the printing and one rubric observation reported by a scholar who cites it as his authority.
stages.witness_label: Missale canonicorum regularium O.S.A. secundum ritum insignis ecclesie Sancti Victoris ad muros Parisienses, Paris, Prévost, 1529
stages.summary: Legg's table of the times at which the chalice is prepared gives, for the canons of Saint-Victor at Paris, the time 'after vesting and before approaching altar', on the authority of this missal; he could not tell whether the rule concerned solemn or private Mass.

evidence.locus: Printed p. 167, table row 'Canons of St. Victor at Paris' (image n218)
evidence.claim: Chalice prepared after vesting and before approaching the altar; solemn or private Mass not determined.

evidence.locus: Parisiensis (S. Victor de Paris) entry
evidence.claim: 15 September 1529, Missale canonicorum regularium ordinis Sancti Augustini secundum ritum ... Sancti Victoris (OCR read).

stages.limitations: One table entry without a folio. The original was not viewed; the day and month come from the bibliography.
stages.reception: Not established beyond the title's designation of Saint-Victor.

stages.label: 1513 Chezal-Benoît missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
stages.date_label: 1513 as cited by Analecta hymnica (title leaf not inspected)
stages.scope: The printed missal as a collated witness of one Christmas sequence.
stages.witness_label: Missale Casalis Benedicti, Rouen 1513 (Analecta hymnica 54, siglum L of no. 102)
stages.summary: Blume and Bannister edit the Christmas sequence 'Laetare, puerpera' (no. 102) and list the Rouen 1513 Chezal-Benoît missal as witness L. It is not among the witnesses they say they did not collate.

evidence.claim: 'Miss. Casalis Benedicti impr. Rotomagi 1513' is witness L of the sequence 'Laetare, puerpera'; only DEIQ are named as not collated.

stages.limitations: Attests one sequence in the book; nothing else about its contents. The original was not viewed. The printer in the label (Martin Morin) and the day (21 March 1513) come from Weale–Bohatta no. 1687; Analecta hymnica gives only 'impr. Rotomagi 1513'.

stages.label: 1527 La Chaise-Dieu missal (Lyon)
stages.date_label: 1527 as cited by Analecta hymnica (title leaf not inspected)
stages.scope: The printed missal as a collated witness of one Marian sequence.
stages.witness_label: Missale Coenobii Casae Dei, Lyon 1527 (Analecta hymnica 54, siglum U of no. 253)
stages.summary: Blume and Bannister edit the Marian sequence 'Res est admirabilis' (no. 253) and list the Lyon 1527 La Chaise-Dieu missal as witness U. It is not among the witnesses they say they did not collate.

evidence.claim: 'Miss. Coenobii Casae Dei impr. Lugduni 1527' is witness U; only GRSV are named as not collated.

stages.limitations: Attests one sequence in the book. The editors cite the same book elsewhere as uncollated. The original was not viewed.

stages.label: 1556 Saint-Remi missal (Reims, Nicolas Bacquenois)
stages.date_label: 1556 as cited by Analecta hymnica (title leaf not inspected)
stages.scope: The printed missal as a collated witness of one Transfiguration sequence.
stages.witness_label: Missale S. Remigii Remensis, Reims 1556 (Analecta hymnica 54, siglum H of no. 108)
stages.summary: Blume and Bannister edit the Transfiguration sequence 'De parente summo natum' (no. 108) and list the Reims 1556 Saint-Remi missal as witness H, citing its readings in the apparatus. Only the 1506 Noyon missal (F) is named as not collated.

evidence.claim: 'Miss. S. Remigii Remensis impr. Remis 1556' is witness H, with variants cited (e.g. 7, 1 and 14, 1); F alone is not collated.

stages.limitations: Attests one sequence in the book. The title's claim that the book was drawn from manuscripts is not checked. The original was not viewed. The printer in the label (Nicolas Bacquenois) and the month (March 1556) come from Weale–Bohatta no. 1704; Analecta hymnica gives only 'impr. Remis 1556'.
